chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to him, 'A man who missed a prayer from the prayers of the journey, and remembered it while in residence.' He said, 'He should make up what he missed as it was missed. If it was a prayer of the journey, he should perform it in residence like it. And if it was a prayer of residence, let him make up the prayer of residence during the journey as it was missed.'
ai.seo_question: How to make up a missed prayer if you were traveling when it was missed but are now at home?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, establishes the principle that the form of the missed prayer (qada) is determined by the traveler's status at the time of the original omission, rather than their current location. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of the legal state (hukm) at the moment of obligation, ensuring that the concession of shortening (qasr) or the requirement of completeness (tamam) remains fixed to the context in which the prayer was neglected. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility of ritual law in response to changing circumstances of travel.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘A man who misses out of a Salāt from the Salāts of the journey, so he remembers it during the staying’. Heasws said: ‘He should fulfil what he missed as if he missed out as if it was a Salāt of the journey. He should pay it back during the staying, the like of it. And if it was a Salāt of the staying (being at home), so let him pay it back during the journey like the Salāt of the staying, just as he had missed it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who misses a Salah (prayer) while on a journey and remembers it when he is at home. He (the Imam) said, ‘He performs Qada’ (compensatory prayer) for it just as it was missed, if missed on a journey the compensatory prayer for it at home is as reduced and if it is missed at home the compensatory prayer for it, if performed on a journey, is complete.’”
